claims.statement: There is a universal decaying envelope rho(s)->0, in particular C s^{-1/2}, for |int exp(i s x^2) f(x) dx| over all probability densities 0<=f<=1.
claims.refutation: For every s>=1 choose a measure-one subset E_s of {x in [12,24]: cos(sx^2)>=1/2}; then f_s=1_{E_s} has modulus at least 1/2.
claims.scope: Refutes only the advertised pointwise oscillatory-decay proof mechanism, not the bounded-density conjecture.

claims.statement: If X has a probability density bounded by 1, then int_R |E exp(i t X^2)|^3 dt <= 16 pi; for lambda!=0 the bound is 16 pi/|lambda|.

For independent coordinates with densities bounded by 1 and a coordinate-diagonal quadratic form having at least three coefficients of absolute value at least 1, the law has a bounded continuous density with sup norm at most 8, for arbitrary signs and arbitrary additional diagonal terms.
Uniformly bound the L1 norm in t of the characteristic function of x^T A x for every product density with one-dimensional factors <=1 whenever the third singular value of A is at least 1.
claims.role: First unpaid implication after the pointwise-decay mechanism is removed.
